text.p: The central bank injected 25 trillion lira overnight cash at 75 percent on Tuesday and stepped into the currency market to curb the dollar's sharp gains amid expectations of excess liquidity for Wednesday.
The lira closed weaker at 97,960 to the dollar against an opening 97,700 despite the central bank's dollar sales, but was firmer on Monday's 98,100 close.

The central bank began selling dollars for lira at around 97,960 lira in the afternoon to suppress a rise triggered by expectations of a cash surplus due to low demand at the Treasury's six-month bill auction.
But the lira weakened further to 98,350 per dollar with tomorrow value after the auction results.
The treasury sold only 69.62 trillion lira of 182-day t-bills, with the yield surging to 135.16 percent, up by 16.41 points up from the previous 273-day bill auction on November 5.
Bankers were earlier expecting thin demand and higher yields in the auction because of a 10 percent withholding tax imposed on state paper to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1.
Banks will pay 44.7 trillion lira to the Treasury for the 182-day bills to be issued on Wednesday when 128.1 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
Nearly 60 trillion lira will be left idle in the system after banks' overnight repayments to the central bank.

Bankers said excess cash could be diverted to the dollar tomorrow, prompting more central bank intervention. They said the sharply higher auction yield would also support upward expectations in t-bill and bond rates.
They said the markets would wait for central bank moves on the U.S. currency's gains and withdrawal of surplus lira tomorrow.
Yields on t-bills and bonds with 1997 maturities which eased ahead of the auction on buying, rose in trade with Wednesday value after the sharply higher auction yield.
The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper jumped to 117.61 percent with Wednesday value after closing at 116.89 percent today, compared to 117.35 percent on Monday.
The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 117.68 percent with Wednesday value, after closing at an average 117.20 percent today and at 117.23 on Monday.
